subject: english-language
title: Language & Power Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the core concepts behind how language carries power.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language & Power walkthrough — Fairclough, instrumental vs influential power.
final_note: You learned Fairclough's two power types and the basics of asymmetrical interactions.

concepts.def: Ability to control or influence others through language
Power that persuades or shapes opinion (ads)
Unequal exchange where one party holds power
Linguist who theorised about language and power
The person with control in an interaction

walkthroughs.body_html: Norman Fairclough split power into instrumental (authority) and influential (persuasion).

A judge sentencing a defendant. A teacher giving detention. A police officer giving an order.

The power comes from ROLE — not from what's said.

An advert, a sermon, a politician's speech, an opinion piece.

No authority — just words shaping minds.

mcqs.q: A judge passing sentence holds what kind of power?
A car advert persuading you to buy uses what kind of power?

numericals.q: How many main types of power did Fairclough identify (instrumental and influential)?

free_texts.q: What's Fairclough's term for power held through ROLE or authority? One word.
free_texts.hint: Same root as 'instrument' — a tool of office.
